questions.q: What tends to happen when a council is assembled by "whoever's available" rather than deliberately?
options: It tends to either rubber-stamp everything or get stuck in constant disagreement
It always produces faster decisions than a deliberate council
It automatically meets more often than necessary
It eliminates the need for an executive sponsor
questions.explain: Without deliberate selection for functional range and real authority, a council lacks what it needs to actually resolve disputes well.

questions.q: What size does the lesson suggest for a working council's voting membership?
options: Roughly six to ten members
At least fifty members for full representation
Exactly two members
As many as possible to be fully inclusive
questions.explain: The lesson describes six to ten voting members as large enough for range but small enough to actually reach decisions.

questions.q: What are the four sections of the agenda structure the lesson describes?
options: Standing items, decisions needed, escalations, new business
Jokes, lunch order, parking, adjournment
Budget, hiring, marketing, sales
Minutes from last year, vendor contracts, holidays, retirement plans
questions.explain: These four sections keep the meeting focused on items with a clear decision attached.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should NOT be on a council or committee agenda?
options: An item with no clear decision attached to it
A policy that needs formal approval
An escalation a working group couldn't resolve
A cross-domain dispute between two data owners
questions.explain: The lesson states items without a clear decision attached belong in a status update, not a meeting agenda.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a decision must be recorded, regardless of whether it was reached by vote or consensus?
options: A decision nobody wrote down gets re-argued from scratch the next time it comes up
Recording decisions is only required for legal compliance in finance
Unrecorded decisions are automatically invalid under any method
Recording is only necessary if the vote was unanimous
questions.explain: The decision log prevents re-litigating settled questions and keeps decisions traceable back to the charter's scope.
